title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
blurb: The Power of Now is a spiritual guide to escaping the endless chatter of the mind. Eckhart Tolle argues that most of our suffering comes not from events but from identifying with our thoughts, especially thoughts about the past and the future. He describes how, after years of anxiety and depression, a sudden shift left him deeply at peace. From that experience he teaches a simple practice: notice the voice in your head instead of obeying it, and bring your attention fully into the present moment. Along the way he explains the ego, the pain-body, the difference between clock time and psychological time, and how sensing your inner body can anchor you. The book ends with surrender, which he frames not as giving up but as accepting what is, then acting from clarity rather than fear.

lessons.b: Tolle's own breakdown and awakening revealed that the constant voice in your head is not who you are, and believing it is the root of most suffering.

lessons.b: Simply observing your thoughts without judging them creates a gap of stillness, and in that gap you discover a calmer awareness behind the mind.
Use clock time for practical plans, but stop living in psychological time, where the mind endlessly replays the past and worries about the future.
